request.spec:
The sheet has terms: a number of days (settings, SETTING_CHANGED key=terms value=<days>), 14
unless changed. A claim's due-by is its date plus the terms in force. A claim is overdue when it
is OPEN and its due-by is before the sheet's today. Show due-by and overdue yes/no on each claim,
and per person and for the sheet an overdue count and overdue-total (the due of the overdue
claims that count).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has terms: a number of days (settings, SETTING_CHANGED key=terms value=<days>), 14
unless changed. A claim's due-by is its date plus the terms in force. A claim is overdue when it
is OPEN and its due-by is before the sheet's today. Show due-by and overdue yes/no on each claim,
and per person and for the sheet an overdue count and overdue-total (the due of the overdue
claims that count).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now has terms, and each claim shows its due-by date and whether it is overdue. Each person and the sheet as a whole show an overdue count and overdue-total. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec. After that run I removed one unneeded type cast in the new front-end file; the type check still passes, but I didn't re-run the e2e tests after that last change.

**Settings (server):** `terms` is stored like the other settings and is 14 when never set. Saving a value writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=terms value=<days>`, after the clerk-limit and floor lines when they're saved together. A blank terms value leaves the terms unchanged. Anything that isn't a whole number of days (0 to 9999) is refused, and nothing is stored or audited.

**One fix to existing behaviour:** before this change, saving the form with the clerk-limit box blank cleared the limit (unless a floor was saved too). Saving only the terms would therefore have wiped the clerk limit. A blank clerk limit now means "no limit" only when nothing else is being saved; with a floor or terms it is left unchanged.

**Settings form:** there is a new terms input (`setting-terms`) and a "Terms in force" display (`setting-terms-current`).

**Overdue figures (front end):** these are worked out in the browser, the same way the existing due figures are, in the new file `features/rates/overdue.slot.tsx`:
- **Due-by** is the claim's date plus the terms. It is shown on every claim, including drafts.
- **Overdue** means the claim is OPEN and its due-by is before the sheet's today. A claim exactly on its due-by date is not overdue.
- **Per person and for the sheet:** the overdue count and overdue-total include only overdue claims that count toward the totals. A held person's OPEN claims are left out, though their own row can still say "yes". A claim with no due figure ("n/a") is counted but adds nothing to the total.

The terms setting applies to all claims and can't be set from a given date, because the spec only sets it undated. No new audit lines are written for overdue figures, because the spec doesn't expect any.
